BARBITURATES (BAR)                                                         -                 Expected Absent

Interpretation

A barbiturate is a drug that acts as a central nervous system depressant and can therefore produce a wide spectrum of effects, from mild sedation to death. Barbiturates are effective as anxiolytics, hypnotics, and anticonvulsants, but have physical and psychological addiction potential.

COCAINE (COC)                                                                    -                 Expected Absent

Interpretation

Cocaine, also known as coke, is a strong stimulant mostly used as a recreational drug. It is commonly snorted, inhaled as smoke, or dissolved and injected into a vein. Mental effects may include loss of contact with reality, an intense feeling of happiness, or agitation.

AMPHETAMINE (AMP)                                                       -                  Expected Absent

Interpretation

Amphetamine is a potent central nervous system stimulant that is used in the treatment of attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, narcolepsy, and obesity. Amphetamine was discovered in 1887 and exists as two enantiomers: levoamphetamine and dextroamphetamine.

Buprenorphine (BUP)                                                           -                 Expected Absent

Interpretation

There are two formulations of buprenorphine available for people on pharmacotherapy treatment in Victoria:

  • Suboxone Sublingual Film® – A combination of buprenorphine and naloxone (also known as Narcan®). This is the most widely used form
  • Subutex Sublingual Tablets® – Contains only buprenorphine2

Tramadol (TRA)                                                                    -                 Expected Absent

Interpretation

Tramadol Warnings. Tramadol may increase your risk of having a seizure. This can occur at a normal dose but is more likely if you take more tramadol than prescribed. You may be at greater risk if you are taking an antidepressant or another opioid pain reliever

Morphine (MOP)                                                                   -               Expected Absent

Interpretation

Morphine is a pain medication of the opiate family which is found naturally in a number of plants and animals. It acts directly on the central nervous system to decrease the feeling of pain. It can be taken for both acute pain and chronic pain

Oxycodone (OXY)                                                                   -               Expected Absent

Interpretation

Oxycodone, sold under the brand name OxyContin among others, is an opioid medication used for the treatment of moderate to severe pain. It is usually taken by mouth and is available in immediate-release and controlled-release formulations

​Propoxyphene (PPX)                                                              -               Expected Absent

Interpretation

Dextropropoxyphene is an analgesic in the opioid category, patented in 1955 and manufactured by Eli Lilly and Company. It is an optical isomer of levopropoxyphene. It is intended to treat mild pain and also has antitussive and local anesthetic effects.

​BENZODIAZEPINES (BZO)                                                    -               Expected Absent

Interpretation

Benzodiazepines, sometimes called "benzos", are a class of psychoactive drugs whose core chemical structure is the fusion of a benzene ring and a diazepine ring.
